findings.title: DynamoDB table without point-in-time recovery
findings.description: Without a point_in_time_recovery block, DynamoDB continuous backups are disabled and the table cannot be restored to an arbitrary point in the preceding 35 days.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: DynamoDB table without customer-managed encryption
findings.description: AWS encrypts DynamoDB tables at rest by default with AWS-owned keys; this rule treats a missing server_side_encryption block as insufficient because AWS-owned keys offer no customer control over key rotation or revocation. Set server_side_encryption { enabled = true, kms_key_arn = ... }.
findings.evidence: server_side_encryption.enabled = absent (AWS-owned key, no customer control)
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: SNS topic without KMS encryption
findings.description: SNS topics should encrypt messages at rest with a KMS key. A topic with no kms_master_key_id relies on unencrypted delivery.
findings.expected: kms_master_key_id set to a KMS key ARN or alias

findings.title: DynamoDB table without deletion protection
findings.description: A DynamoDB table without deletion_protection_enabled can be deleted by anyone with table-management permissions.
